flows.summary: Point flowmap at a repo and get the mechanical list of every entry point, then make sure the call graph can walk from each one.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap inventory` to list every entry point into inventory.json
steps.notes: adapters/__init__.py:entries dispatches per [[entry]] to fastapi/rails/nextjs/cli/pattern/list adapters; this repo's flowmap.toml uses cli. Without flowmap.toml, config.py:detect_entries guesses adapters.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap callgraph check` to confirm every entry point's handler is a call-graph node
steps.notes: Same command also has `flowmap callgraph` (count defs/edges) and `callgraph dump [ref]` (graph JSON, via lens.graph_at); exits 1 on any broken handler.

flows.summary: Hand out briefs for several independent bottom-up/top-down passes and check each pass's citations and coverage.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap brief <run-id> <method>` to write a brief for each independent pass
steps.notes: Fills the RUN_SPEC.md template with METHODS/STACK text and the flow vocabulary (discovery mode when empty).

steps.name: An agent follows its brief and writes its run JSON
steps.notes: Done outside the CLI (the flowmap-build skill fans out agents); no entry point or code path.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap verify` to reject invented citations and list unplaced entry points

flows.summary: Vote the independent passes into one map and settle the disagreements a human must decide.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap reconcile` to vote the passes into map.json, MAP.md and QUESTIONS.md
Maintainer names the proposed flows in flowmap.toml, pins split votes in decisions.json, and reconciles again
steps.notes: flowmap.toml and decisions.json are edited by hand; reconcile only reads them (pinned endpoint_flow, confirmed_steps, vocabulary renames new:* ids).

flows.summary: Look at the reconciled map as Mermaid diagrams, the interactive atlas, or the left-to-right canvas.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap diagrams` to write Mermaid at system, flow and step zoom
Maintainer runs `flowmap atlas` to build the interactive atlas page
steps.notes: The page itself is atlas.template.html with data injected; build() is its generator.

steps.name: Maintainer runs `flowmap canvas` to draw the map as one left-to-right picture
steps.notes: --from <atlas.html> skips building and re-reads the data embedded in an existing atlas page (canvas.py:from_page).

flows.summary: Place a PR or commit range on the map: which flows and steps it touches, what it reaches, and what the lens can't see.

steps.name: Reviewer runs `flowmap lens <base> <head>` to get the verdict, touched steps, reach and blind spots
After `git push` / `gh pr create` in Claude Code, the PR hook runs lens on the open PR and hands it to Claude to post one comment
steps.notes: bin/flowmap-pr-hook is not in the inventory (it lives in bin/, not the commands dir) but shells out to `flowmap lens`; `post` creates/edits the PR comment via gh.

steps.name: Reviewer runs `flowmap callgraph impact <file:sym>` to see which entry points and flows can reach a symbol
Reviewer runs `flowmap atlas --pr base..head=label` to paint a change's reach onto the atlas
Reviewer runs `flowmap canvas --change name=base..head` to paint a change and its story chapters onto the canvas
steps.notes: Reads docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json when present to number chapters on cards.

flows.summary: Tell a PR as chapters on the map: gather facts, check the story against them, render the change page and a shareable link.

steps.name: Author runs `flowmap change <base> <head> --facts` to get the deterministic facts a story is written from
steps.notes: The author (usually the pr-lens skill) then writes docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json by hand.

steps.name: Author runs `flowmap change ... --check` to list the story's claims the facts don't back
steps.notes: Writes nothing; prints JSON problems and exits 1 if any.

steps.name: Author runs `flowmap change <base> <head> --name pr-<n>` to render the change page
Author adds `--link` to get a viewer link carrying the whole page in its fragment for the PR body
Admin runs `flowmap viewer <dir>` to build a self-hosted copy of the change viewer
steps.notes: Optional: --link defaults to the hosted viewer at flowmap.testabl.ai; `viewer` in flowmap.toml or FLOWMAP_VIEWER points links at the self-hosted copy.

observations: Three separate derivations of 'which symbols changed': flowmap/lens.py:analyse (drops docstring/format-only edits via flowmap/lens.py:cosmetic), flowmap/change.py:facts (no cosmetic filter, adds new/deleted/modified status) and flowmap/atlas.py:overlay (no cosmetic filter, new vs changed by base defs). A change page can list a symbol whose edit the verdict on the same page ignored.

flowmap/change.py:facts calls flowmap/lens.py:analyse in full just to read verdict/blind/spreads_to, after already recomputing changed lines, graphs and endpoint sets itself; flowmap/canvas.py:main does the same per --change on top of flowmap/atlas.py:overlay. `flowmap change` is busier than its intent ('render a page') because it is lens plus a second lens.

flowmap/atlas.py:data builds the call graph from the working tree (flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.__init__ -> flowmap/callgraph.py:Graph.__init__) while flowmap/atlas.py:overlay uses flowmap/lens.py:graph_at(head) from git; one atlas page can mix two graphs when the worktree differs from head.

flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes reads the reconciler's split votes back by regex-parsing the generated QUESTIONS.md prose instead of structured data from flowmap/reconcile.py:main: a markdown wording change in flowmap/reconcile.py:write_questions_md silently empties the atlas's split badges.

flowmap/change.py imports flowmap/atlas.py:step_keys, which pulls in flowmap/diagrams.py (module-level config reads, Diagrams) just for a tiny key helper: the change command depends on the atlas/diagram stack.

flowmap/lens.py:endpoint_set records failures into the module-global INVENTORY_ERRORS that flowmap/lens.py:blind_spots later reads; since flowmap/change.py:facts calls endpoint_set itself and then lens.analyse, state from one call leaks into the next analysis in the same process.

flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.write hardcodes '`executor.run_workflow`' in the generated README text regardless of the configured [flows].engine, and generated docs still say 'tools/flowmap/...'; leftovers from the app the tool was first built in.

Two lists of commands must stay in sync: bin/flowmap's COMMANDS set dispatches via runpy, while the inventory derives commands from every flowmap/*.py with a __main__ block (flowmap/adapters/cli.py:entries); bin/flowmap-pr-hook, the only automatic caller, is not an entry point at all.
flowmap/change.py:main writes the HTML page before refusing --link on story lint problems, so a 'refused' run still overwrites docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.html.
